parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents state actors as the principal threat: police are identified (with police and the human-rights commission acknowledging it) as the foremost perpetrators of violations against LGBTI people — systematic harassment, arbitrary detention, assault and extortion using the threat of arrest under ss.365/365A, plus forced anal/vaginal examinations (torture). Vagrancy and 'cheating by personation' provisions are listed as criminalising trans gender expression, reaching a visitor whose documents mismatch presentation. Recourse is thin: no anti-discrimination law, complaints routinely ignored. Custody defaults to birth-sex placement with no dedicated housing. Care settings involve ridicule. Protections are climate signals only (2016 certification, limited prosecutions, supportive head-of-state statement, civil society). No documented killings, but state-directed targeting dominates.

entry_documents.exposure: Vagrancy and 'cheating by personation' provisions listed as criminalising trans gender expression; document/presentation mismatch could feed a personation allegation. No documented border practice for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry refusal or marker policy; prosecutions under ss.365/365A reported limited (though 2012 conviction data is stale).
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → police encounter → personation or ss.365 threat used as extortion/detention lever.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police documented as foremost perpetrators of systematic harassment, arbitrary detention, assault and extortion of LGBTI people; forced anal/vaginal examinations used to seek evidence of same-sex conduct (torture). Custody placement defaults to birth sex; no dedicated trans housing (Oct 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Placement considers recognised card/doctor assessment 'where possible'; prisoners'-rights committee advocacy. No statutory placement rule.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing during any stop → arrest threat → examination/detention → birth-sex ward exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Birth-sex ward placement is the practical default in the current male/female system; officials cite distrust of trans identification as reason to resist gender-based placement — tier-1 state exposure in custody.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Case-by-case discretion; recognised-ID holders accommodated by preferred gender where possible; future prisons planned to have separate space.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Police detention or any custodial episode immediately triggers this placement rule.

care_services.exposure: Medical staff report ignorance, curiosity and ridicule when gender care is sought; hormone therapy described as fraught; patients avoid public facilities. Blood service bars MSM (tangential).
care_services.protection: No documented denial of emergency care to trans visitors; gender-recognition circular exists.
care_services.interaction: Illness/injury forcing disclosure → ward placement and staff hostility; HRT continuity uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: ss.365/365A 'pave the way' for branding LGBT people perverts and criminals; police and anti-gay groups use them to justify harassment and moral policing in public and private; police ignore LGBTQ victims' complaints.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No convictions found (2012); prosecutions limited (2026); head of state's 2021 dignity statement; professional colleges call for decriminalisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute operates as police leverage rather than prosecution — the everyday exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Conversion 'treatment' sought by families is a resident/family-context signal with no documented traveller-with-minor scenario; elevated penalty where offence involves a person under 16 concerns same-sex conduct, not trans identity.
minors_guardians.protection: Professional college ethics condemn conversion practice; no youth-specific findings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or killing count documented. Police response documented as hostile: complaints ignored, extortion and assault by officers, threats of arrest used against LGBTQIA individuals.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Community organisations exist (support groups founded 1994/1999, equality organisation); NGO coalition reporting; 72.5% poll support for non-punishment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Seeking police help after any incident risks re-exposure and extortion rather than protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive anti-discrimination protection; police identified as primary violators with only administrative circulars in place; independent HR commission acknowledged police abuses without documented remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Gender-recognition circular (2016); UPR stakeholder reporting; foreign asylum policy note; some political-party support; influential Buddhist chapter backing rights extension.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are resident-facing or diplomatic; a short-stay visitor has no effective complaint route against police.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A. Vellandra's regime is exclusion and humiliation at the border with no arrest; this dossier documents state agents themselves assaulting, extorting and detaining LGBT people, plus forced examinations (torture) and custody placement by birth sex — more severe, state-perpetrated harms, not merely refusal of entry.

Closest match. Varnalia 0.25-A features routine police raids, detention, fines, extortion and slow courts with rare imprisonment; here likewise systematic police harassment/extortion/arbitrary detention with limited prosecutions and weak remedy. This case lacks documented regular raids but adds forced examinations and birth-sex custody, keeping it at the lower edge of that tier.

Materially higher than this dossier. Kestrel Isles' exposure is discretionary secondary screening and refused admission with written appeal and consular notification, no state abuse. This jurisdiction documents police as systematic perpetrators, extortion via arrest threats and torture-adjacent examinations — a different tier of state conduct, so it rates well below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one where the state is the principal actor producing risk. Criminal provisions aimed at same-sex conduct, though rarely prosecuted, function daily as police leverage: harassment, extortion and assault using the threat of arrest are documented as systematic and acknowledged by the police and human-rights commission themselves, alongside forced examinations amounting to torture. Vagrancy and personation provisions extend criminal framing to trans gender expression, directly relevant to a visitor whose documents mismatch presentation, and any custody episode defaults to birth-sex placement with no dedicated housing. Recourse is thin — no anti-discrimination law, complaints ignored — so rule of law operates as a liability, not protection. Mitigating signals (2016 certification, limited prosecutions, supportive official statements, civil society) are climate indicators and do not offset the documented state-perpetrated exposure.
